_comment: The forms that figure, parallelism and contrast notes in config/figures/ may use. Shown only at Deep.
label is the plain name a reader sees first; term is the usual name for the form; about says what it is in plain words.

defined, where present, is the form defined in the words of a book that defines it: source is an id in config/layer-sources.json (which says who wrote its words), quote its exact words, at where in the book, url the page they are on, read the edition or site the words were read from and retrieved the date (decision 10). Pages of Bullinger's Figures of Speech Used in the Bible (1898) are the printed pages of the archive.org scan figuresofspeechu00bull.

quotable lists the cite-list ids whose words may be shown in a figure note: public-domain works whose words are their named writer's own, in a copy free to quote. Left out, per docs/local-work/2026-10-20/voices/VOICES-SHORTLIST.md as the founder approved it: Gill and Spurgeon (the only typed texts are editors' with rights reserved; Spurgeon waits for Project Gutenberg's proofread volumes, decision 8), the Geneva notes (no free-to-copy statement, and a modern editor's notes mixed in), the Companion Bible (its one typed copy has no license and garbles letters, and it was completed after Bullinger's death in 1913 by others, in parts not yet established), Henry's Concise and Wesley (abridgments, much of them in Henry's, Poole's or Bengel's words), the church fathers (a group, not one work) and the Pulpit Commentary (Bible Hub's text carries BibleSoft's copyright notice; it may be cited and linked, never quoted). Tropologia is left out too (2026-11-01): Book I is partly translated and compiled from other writers, and Books II and III hold other men's poems. The NET translators' notes are never shown. Works left out may still be linked from Layers.

A cite or definition names no writer itself: the cite list in config/layer-sources.json says who wrote a source's words on each book, as it does for Layers (decision 10), so a work by several hands credits each book's own writer, two works by one writer count once toward a note's strength, and words whose writer is not named or is no longer cited are refused.

forms.label: Said twice
forms.about: The second line says the first again in other words.

defined.quote: This is when the lines are parallel in thought, and in the use of synonymous words.
defined.read: the UniqueBible.app module of the 1898 text, at github.com/darrelwright/UniqueBible_Books (commit 4017a67)

forms.label: Opposite lines
forms.about: The second line answers the first with its opposite.

defined.quote: This is when the words are contrasted in the two or more lines, being opposed in sense the one to the other.
defined.read: the UniqueBible.app module of the 1898 text, at github.com/darrelwright/UniqueBible_Books (commit 4017a67)

forms.label: Lines that build
forms.about: Each line is built the same way, or adds to the line before it.

defined.quote: This is where the parallelism consists only in the similar form of construction
defined.read: the UniqueBible.app module of the 1898 text, at github.com/darrelwright/UniqueBible_Books (commit 4017a67)

forms.label: Mirror
forms.about: Words or lines go out in one order and come back in the reverse order.

defined.quote: This is when the parallel lines are so placed that if there be six lines, the first corresponds with the sixth, the second with the fifth, and the third with the fourth.
defined.read: the UniqueBible.app module of the 1898 text, at github.com/darrelwright/UniqueBible_Books (commit 4017a67)

forms.label: Lines that take turns
forms.about: The lines take turns: the first answers the third, and the second the fourth.

defined.quote: it is alternate when, of the four members, the first corresponds with the third, and the second with the fourth.
defined.read: the UniqueBible.app module of the 1898 text, at github.com/darrelwright/UniqueBible_Books (commit 4017a67)

forms.label: Lines that climb
forms.about: Each line goes a step higher than the one before it, often taking up its words.

defined.quote: The Figure is so called when a writing, speech, or discourse, ascends up step by step, each with an increase of emphasis or sense.
defined.read: the UniqueBible.app module of the 1898 text, at github.com/darrelwright/UniqueBible_Books (commit 4017a67)

forms.label: Bookends
forms.about: A passage begins and ends with the same words, which frame what lies between.

defined.quote: The Latins called it INCLUSIO, inclusion: either because the first word of the sentence is included at the end, or because of the importance of the matter which is thus included between the two words.
defined.read: the UniqueBible.app module of the 1898 text, at github.com/darrelwright/UniqueBible_Books (commit 4017a67)

forms.label: A refrain
forms.about: The same line comes back again and again through a passage.

defined.quote: The figure is so called because the sentence or phrase is repeated at intervals, as though in regular circles.
defined.read: the UniqueBible.app module of the 1898 text, at github.com/darrelwright/UniqueBible_Books (commit 4017a67)

forms.label: Lines that begin alike
forms.about: Line after line begins with the same word or words, to add weight.

defined.quote: This figure is so-called because it is the repeating of the same word at the beginning of successive clauses: thus adding weight and emphasis to statements and arguments by calling special attention to them.
defined.read: the UniqueBible.app module of the 1898 text, at github.com/darrelwright/UniqueBible_Books (commit 4017a67)

forms.label: One thing named for another
forms.about: One thing is named in place of another it goes with, such as a cause for its effect.

defined.quote: Metonymy is a figure by which one name or noun is used instead of another, to which it stands in a certain relation.
defined.read: the UniqueBible.app module of the 1898 text, at github.com/darrelwright/UniqueBible_Books (commit 4017a67)

forms.label: A part for the whole
forms.about: A part is named for the whole, or the whole for a part.

defined.quote: A figure by which one word receives something from another which is internally associated with it by the connection of two ideas: as when a part of a thing is put by a kind of Metonymy for the whole of it, or the whole for a part.
defined.read: the UniqueBible.app module of the 1898 text, at github.com/darrelwright/UniqueBible_Books (commit 4017a67)

forms.label: God in human terms
forms.about: Human feelings, actions or parts are spoken of God, so that we can understand Him.

defined.quote: This figure is used of the ascription of human passions, actions, or attributes to God.
defined.read: the UniqueBible.app module of the 1898 text, at github.com/darrelwright/UniqueBible_Books (commit 4017a67)

forms.label: Things spoken of as persons
forms.about: Things or ideas are spoken of, or spoken to, as if they were persons.

defined.quote: A figure by which things are represented or spoken of as persons
defined.read: the UniqueBible.app module of the 1898 text, at github.com/darrelwright/UniqueBible_Books (commit 4017a67)

forms.label: Like this
forms.about: One thing is said to be like another.

defined.quote: A Declaration that one Thing resembles another; or, Comparison by Resemblance
defined.read: the UniqueBible.app module of the 1898 text, at github.com/darrelwright/UniqueBible_Books (commit 4017a67)

forms.label: This is that
forms.about: One thing is said to be another, to show what it is like.

defined.quote: A Declaration that one Thing is (or represents) another; or, Comparison by Representation
defined.read: the UniqueBible.app module of the 1898 text, at github.com/darrelwright/UniqueBible_Books (commit 4017a67)

forms.label: A number, then one more
forms.about: A number is named and then the next one up, to give the point more force.

forms.label: Speaking to the absent
forms.about: The speaker turns from his hearers to speak to someone or something not there, such as the heavens.

defined.quote: The figure is so called when the speaker turns away from the real auditory whom he is addressing, and speaks to an imaginary one.
defined.read: the UniqueBible.app module of the 1898 text, at github.com/darrelwright/UniqueBible_Books (commit 4017a67)

forms.label: More than literal
forms.about: More is said than is meant literally, to make the point strongly.

defined.quote: when more is said than is meant to be literally understood, in order to heighten the sense.
defined.read: the UniqueBible.app module of the 1898 text, at github.com/darrelwright/UniqueBible_Books (commit 4017a67)

forms.label: Saying the opposite
forms.about: The words say the opposite of what is meant, to give the point more force.

defined.quote: The figure is so called when the speaker intends to convey a sense contrary to the strict signification of the words employed
defined.read: the UniqueBible.app module of the 1898 text, at github.com/darrelwright/UniqueBible_Books (commit 4017a67)

forms.label: A question that tells
forms.about: A question is asked not to learn anything but to make a point.

defined.quote: This figure is used when a speaker or writer asks animated questions, but not to obtain information.
defined.read: the UniqueBible.app module of the 1898 text, at github.com/darrelwright/UniqueBible_Books (commit 4017a67)

forms.label: A doubled word
forms.about: A word is said twice in a row, for weight or feeling.

defined.quote: It is a common and powerful way of emphasizing a particular word, by thus marking it and calling attention to it.
defined.read: the UniqueBible.app module of the 1898 text, at github.com/darrelwright/UniqueBible_Books (commit 4017a67)

forms.label: One word in two forms
forms.about: A word is repeated in another form, such as a verb with its own noun, for emphasis.

defined.quote: Polyptoton means with many cases, i.e., a repetition of the same noun in several cases, or of the same verb in several moods or tenses.
defined.read: the UniqueBible.app module of the 1898 text, at github.com/darrelwright/UniqueBible_Books (commit 4017a67)

forms.label: A gentle word
forms.about: A hard or unpleasant thing is said in a gentler way.

defined.quote: Euphemy is a figure by which a harsh or disagreeable expression is changed for a pleasant and agreeable one
defined.read: the UniqueBible.app module of the 1898 text, at github.com/darrelwright/UniqueBible_Books (commit 4017a67)

forms.label: Two words, one idea
forms.about: Two words joined by "and" name one thing.

defined.quote: Two words employed, but only one thing, or idea, intended.
defined.at: Hendiadys, or Two for One, p. 657
defined.read: the UniqueBible.app module of the 1898 text, at github.com/darrelwright/UniqueBible_Books (commit 4017a67)

forms.label: Seems foolish, is wise
forms.about: Words that seem to clash, or seem foolish at first, prove to be wise.

defined.quote: This is a figure, in which what is said at first sight appears to be foolish, yet when we come to consider it, we find it exceedingly wise.
defined.read: the UniqueBible.app module of the 1898 text, at github.com/darrelwright/UniqueBible_Books (commit 4017a67)

forms.label: Saying less to mean more
forms.about: Less is said than is meant, so that the point is made more strongly.

defined.quote: in Tapeinosis the thing that is lessened is the same thing which is increased and intensified.
defined.read: the UniqueBible.app module of the 1898 text, at github.com/darrelwright/UniqueBible_Books (commit 4017a67)

forms.label: And, and, and
forms.about: "And" is said again and again, so that each thing is weighed on its own.

defined.quote: Instead of hurrying us on, breathlessly, to reach the important conclusion; we are asked to stop at each point
defined.read: the UniqueBible.app module of the 1898 text, at github.com/darrelwright/UniqueBible_Books (commit 4017a67)

forms.label: Without "and"
forms.about: The "and" is left out, hurrying the reader on to what comes last.

defined.quote: When the figure Asyndeton is used, we are not detained over the separate statements, and asked to consider each in detail, but we are hurried on over the various matters that are mentioned
defined.read: the UniqueBible.app module of the 1898 text, at github.com/darrelwright/UniqueBible_Books (commit 4017a67)

forms.label: Set side by side
forms.about: Two people are set side by side, and each shows up the other.

forms.label: Alike
forms.about: Two people are set side by side because one is like the other.
